question: does many_then_trim's trim remove vertices his own recorded move needs?
reading: if the trim preserves all 30, the binding constraint is the ordering or the cap and a bigger knob would have found it; if it removes any, then `many_then_trim` cannot express his own recorded move AT ANY CAP, which is a fact about his second published strategy rather than about our implementation of it
monotonicity_note: adding vertices can never raise w*, and his 30 give w* = 373, so EVERY superset of them reaches 374 -- which is why the rule's failure is omission and why over-proposing can cost only time, never correctness
